title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building the combinatorics of the boundary of the compactified moduli spaces M̄_{g,ν}. The graphs involved are dual graphs of stable curves; the next page calls them 'MD-graphes', presumably Mumford–Deligne graphs. A graph G' has vertex set S', edge set A' and arc set Ã', where arcs are oriented edges (half-edges), and σ_{Ã'} is the involution reversing orientation, so that A' = Ã'/σ.

A 'generalized morphism' of graphs G' → G may send some arcs to identities at vertices, i.e. collapse edges. On the previous page:
- B̃' ⊂ Ã' is the set of arcs that are not collapsed; they map bijectively onto Ã.
- G'_• is the subgraph on all vertices of G' whose edges are the collapsed ones.
- The vertex set is S = π_0(G'_•).
- G is the pushout (52) of S ← G'_• ↪ G' in the category of graphs with generalized morphisms.

On this page:
- (53) names the collapsed arcs C̃' = Ã' \ B̃' and the collapsed edges C' = A' \ B' = C̃'/σ.
- (54) introduces the notation G = G'/C' (and G̃ = G̃'/C̃'). Grothendieck says G is 'deduced from G' by contracting the edges of C' to points'.
- He justifies the terminology through topological realizations: a generalized morphism is realized by a continuous map that collapses certain edges to points.
- He observes that the pushout exists for every spanning subgraph G'_0 of G', equivalently for every edge subset C' ⊂ A'.
- He begins to deduce, finishing on the next page (55), that every generalized morphism factors uniquely as a contraction G' → G'/C' followed by an ordinary graph morphism. Here C' is the set of edges the morphism collapses.

The next page lifts this to MD-graphs. The legs I' → S' are pushed forward. The genus attached to a vertex α of the contracted graph is g_α = Σ_{α'} g'_{α'} + h^1(G'(α)), the sum of the genera of the collapsed vertices plus the first Betti number of the collapsed subgraph. This is the standard rule for edge contraction of stable graphs, i.e. how boundary strata of M̄_{g,n} specialize.

Purpose: to set up the poset or category of degenerations (stratification 'at infinity') of M̄_{g,ν} via contraction morphisms of stable graphs.
errors: Minor internal reference slip: the text cites the pushout as '(57)', but the pushout is diagram (52) on the previous page, and no (57) exists yet. This may be a misreading of the handwriting or a slip of Grothendieck's pen.

Possible notational tension with the previous page. B̃' denotes the arcs that are not contracted, so the contracted subgraph G'_• (= G'_0) has edge set C'. 'Contracting C'' is therefore consistent, but the reader must remember that G'_0 carries the contracted edges, not B'. No mathematical error.

ideas.what: Edge contraction G'/C' realized as a pushout of S=π0(G'_0) ← G'_0 ↪ G' in graphs with generalized (edge-collapsing) morphisms; it exists for any edge subset
ideas.modern_name: Edge contraction / quotient graph; colimits in categories of graphs with contractions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical graph theory. The categorical setting for stable graphs is due to Kontsevich (1994–95), Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998), and Borisov–Manin / Joyal–Kock (Feynman categories of graphs)

ideas.what: Unique factorization of a generalized graph morphism as a contraction followed by an ordinary morphism
ideas.modern_name: (Contraction, ordinary morphism) factorization system on graph morphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Getzler–Kapranov and Behrend–Manin; made explicit in Borisov–Manin (2008) and Joyal–Kock (2011)

ideas.what: Topological interpretation: generalized morphisms are continuous maps of geometric realizations collapsing some edges to points
ideas.modern_name: Geometric realization of graph contractions (homotopy equivalence when contracting forests)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine foundational bookkeeping: edge contraction as a pushout, plus a factorization of generalized morphisms. It is standard in the later literature on stable graphs and modular operads. It is historically mildly interesting that Grothendieck set up this categorical framework for the boundary of M̄_{g,ν} independently, but nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: 'la somme amalgamée (57)' should almost certainly refer to (52), the pushout diagram of the previous page.
'qui contractent [-justes-][?]' most likely reads 'qui contractent justement certaines arêtes en des pts'.

'l'ens. de' [-fléchées-] {+arêtes+} C' ⊂ A' de G'' — read 'l'ens. des arêtes C' ⊂ A' de G''. The crossed-out word appears to be something like 'flèches' or 'fléchées'; the replacement written above is 'arêtes'.
'ayant mêmes sommets que G'' could also be 'ayant les sommets de G''; the meaning is a spanning subgraph either way.
